decisions.thought: Opponent threats: Volcarona (fire/bug, strong special), Dragonite, Gholdengo (Good as Gold blocks my status moves like Parting Shot), Annihilape, Kingambit, Rotom-Wash. Leading with Incineroar for Intimidate and Fake Out. Garchomp and Kingambit are the main physical breakers. Gholdengo and Azumarill are on the bench. Expect the opponent to lead something aggressive; watch for Volcarona's fire attacks on Kingambit.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Incineroar facing Gholdengo, status moves like Parting Shot won't work since Good as Gold blocks them. Flare Blitz hits Steel hard, and Dark Lariat is super effective against Gholdengo's Ghost typing, so I'm weighing which attack maximizes damage here.

Flare Blitz does more raw damage (120 BP) but costs 33% recoil, while Darkest Lariat (85 BP) ignores stat drops and has no recoil but less damage. Since Gholdengo's physical bulk is lower than special, and it'll likely hit back with Make It Rain or Shadow Ball before I can act, I'll go with Flare Blitz to maximize the hit despite the recoil cost.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Kingambit is burned and at low HP against an active Dragonite, with Rotom-Wash benched at 20%. I'm weighing whether Kowtow Cleave hits neutrally since Dark isn't super effective against Dragon/Flying.

I'm calculating that Dragonite's Outrage would hit Kingambit for neutral damage too since Steel doesn't resist Dragon, so staying in risks a big hit. Switching to Garchomp could work since Dragonite's Ground-type Earthquake would be nullified by its Flying typing, though I need to check if Dragonite's own moves threaten Garchomp.

Kingambit is slower so Dragonite strikes first, and with only 104 HP it's vulnerable to chip and burn damage over time. I'm also weighing Gholdengo as a potential switch-in, since Steel/Dark Kingambit resists Ghost-type Shadow Ball, making that matchup less threatening.

Weighing Kowtow Cleave for max damage against Dragonite now versus switching to Garchomp, which can tank a hit and answer back with Stone Edge for solid damage over successive turns.

Garchomp at 109/185 outspeeds Dragonite at 169 speed, with Dragonite sitting at 84% HP so Multiscale wouldn't be active. Checking the type matchups - Stone Edge hits Dragonite's Flying typing super effectively while being neutral against Dragon, whereas Dragon Claw would be super effective against the Dragon typing but neutral against Flying.

Mega Garchomp keeps its speed about the same but gets a big Attack boost to 170 base, making Dragonclaw hit much harder than before. I'll go with Mega Dragonclaw here.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp fainted to Gholdengo's Make It Rain. Opponent left: Gholdengo (full HP, immune to status, SpA now -2), Dragonite (84%, Earthquake threatens Kingambit and Incineroar), Volcarona, Annihilape (unseen). Kingambit (104, burned) is the better switch: Dark/Steel resists Make It Rain, and Kowtow Cleave is 2x on Gholdengo. Plan: Kowtow Cleave Gholdengo, keep Incineroar (80) for Dragonite or a Fire-type threat, and avoid Dragonite's Earthquake.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Garchomp down, I'm weighing Kingambit (burned, holding Black Glasses) against Incineroar to deal with Gholdengo, considering that its Dark-type moves won't hit the Ghost typing effectively while Gholdengo's SpA is lowered from Make It Rain. I'm also keeping Dragonite's health in mind as a lingering threat.

Dragonite's Earthquake would also hit Incineroar hard given its Fire typing, with Dark neutral to Ground. Working out Kowtow Cleave's damage on Gholdengo with its lowered SpA, factoring in Kingambit's high Attack against Gholdengo's Defense plus the ongoing burn, and tallying both Pokémon's remaining HP totals.

Checking speed order, Gholdengo outpaces Kingambit, and Make It Rain against Kingambit's Dark typing would only do resisted damage. Since Kowtow Cleave never misses and suits this matchup better than Sucker Punch against a special attacker, I'm settling on Kingambit as my switch-in since that's the only legal action available right now.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Kingambit is burned and down to about half HP, up against a full-health Gholdengo with its special attack lowered twice. I'm working out whether Make It Rain, a steel-type special move, actually hits Kingambit hard given its Dark/Steel typing and solid special defense—steel-on-steel should only do half damage.

Now I'm calculating Kowtow Cleave's damage: it's super effective against Gholdengo's Ghost typing, boosted by STAB, Supreme Overlord from a fainted ally, and an item like Black Glasses, stacking up to roughly 220+ damage against Gholdengo's HP pool in the 160-190 range, which could be close to a KO.

But if Kingambit is burned, physical damage halves, cutting that estimate down significantly and possibly preventing the KO. I'm also weighing whether Sucker Punch is viable here—it only works if Gholdengo is attacking that turn—and considering the speed matchup, since Gholdengo likely outspeeds Kingambit and would hit first with Make It Rain, which Steel resists somewhat.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Kingambit is at 92 HP and burned, while Dragonite at 47% just revealed Earthquake, which hits Kingambit's Steel typing super effectively since Dark doesn't resist Ground. I'm estimating the damage from Dragonite's Earthquake given its attack stat against Kingambit's defense.

Earthquake could do significant damage but likely not a KO given Kingambit's bulk, while Kowtow Cleave from Kingambit, boosted by Supreme Overlord and Black Glasses, could hit Dragonite hard — potentially enough to knock it out given its weakened HP. Since Dragonite outspeeds Kingambit, it moves first with Earthquake, then Kingambit retaliates with Kowtow Cleave, so the key question is whether Kingambit survives Earthquake's hit while burned before it can strike back.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking Earthquake's effectiveness against Incineroar's Fire/Dark typing - Ground is super effective against Fire, so Incineroar takes double damage from Dragonite's Earthquake.

For Incineroar's options, Flare Blitz is resisted by Dragonite's typing so that's a poor choice, while Darkest Lariat hits neutrally and ignores stat changes. Fake Out could flinch Dragonite before it attacks since priority goes first, giving Incineroar a way to prevent damage this turn.

Actually with only three mons brought and Garchomp, Kingambit already fainted, Parting Shot has no switch target so it'd fail. Best bet seems Darkest Lariat for max damage now, though a Fake Out flinch first to buy a turn then follow up with EQ next turn could also threaten the KO since Dragonite outspeeds and Earthquake likely finishes Incineroar.
